Cock-a-Leekie Soup

Served at: Burns Night Supper

Serves 6-8Prep 25 minCook 1 hour 30 min

Cock-a-Leekie Soup is a classic Scottish broth, traditionally served as a hearty starter for a Burns Night Supper. This warming and flavorful soup combines tender chicken, sweet leeks, and often a hint of sweetness from prunes, embodying the spirit of Scottish comfort food perfect for a cold January evening.

Ingredients

  • 1 whole chicken (about 3-4 lbs / 1.4-1.8 kg), cut into pieces or 6-8 chicken thighs/drumsticks
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil or butter
  • 4 large leeks, white and light green parts only, thinly sliced and thoroughly washed
  • 2 carrots, peeled and diced
  • 2 celery stalks, diced
  • 8 cups (2 liters) chicken stock, homemade or good quality store-bought
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) pearl barley, rinsed
  • 1/2 cup (75 g) pitted prunes, halved (optional, but traditional)
  • 1 bay leaf
  • 1 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves (or 1/2 teaspoon dried)
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
  • Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish

Method

  1. Pat the chicken pieces dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
  2. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil or butter over medium-high heat. Add the chicken pieces and brown them on all sides. You may need to do this in batches to avoid overcrowding the pot. Remove the browned chicken and set aside.
  3. Reduce the heat to medium. Add the sliced leeks, diced carrots, and diced celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables have softened.
  4. Return the browned chicken to the pot. Pour in the chicken stock, ensuring the chicken is mostly submerged. Add the rinsed pearl barley, bay leaf, and thyme.
  5. Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1 hour, or until the chicken is very tender and cooked through.
  6. Carefully remove the chicken pieces from the pot. Once cool enough to handle, remove the meat from the bones and shred or dice it into bite-sized pieces. Discard the bones and skin.
  7. While the chicken cools, add the halved prunes (if using) to the soup. Continue to simmer for another 15-20 minutes, allowing the barley to fully cook and the flavors to meld.
  8. Return the shredded chicken meat to the pot. Stir well and heat through for a few minutes.
  9. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
  10. Ladle the hot soup into bowls, garnish with fresh chopped parsley, and serve immediately.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, use a whole chicken and make your own stock directly in the pot.
  • If you prefer a thicker soup, you can mash some of the cooked barley and vegetables against the side of the pot with a spoon.
  • Leftover soup can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days and reheats well.
